tapeLine: US stocks ended barely higher Thursday as Treasury yields retreated from multiyear highs: the S&P 500 added 0.19% to 7,666.45, the Nasdaq Composite 0.04% to 26,871.60 and the Dow 20.51 points (0.04%) to 50,926.56, per the Washington Post and Yahoo Finance reports. The 10-year yield touched 5.344%, its highest since 2002, before easing to about 5.243%, per CNBC. Friday morning futures pointed higher ahead of the September jobs report (08:30 ET): Dow and S&P 500 futures +0.3%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.6%, per Yahoo Finance and TheStreet.
matters:
Thursday's data leaned firm. Initial jobless claims slipped to 197,000 for the week ended 26 September against 200,000 expected, with continuing claims at a three-year low, per Reuters-based reports. The ISM Manufacturing PMI read 54.5 in September versus 54.6 in August, with the prices index jumping to 77.9 from 71.1, per ISM via PR Newswire. Yields eased from their highs but the 10-year remains above 5.2%.

Today's September jobs report is the next test: the Dow Jones consensus is for +84,000 payrolls and unemployment holding at 4.1%, after +162,000 in August, per CNBC/Yahoo reports; other surveys put the forecast between 88,000 and 100,000. Options pricing implies roughly a 0.9% move for SPY through Friday's expiration, per Yahoo Finance. Reports note the Fed raised rates about two weeks ago; the 28 October FOMC is the next decision point.

Invalidation: the payrolls and unemployment prints, average hourly earnings (+0.3% m/m expected), the 10-year's behaviour after the report, and the contents of the US reply to Iran, still undisclosed in sources found.

scorecard.text: Thursday's brief cited early futures up (Nasdaq 100 +1.0%, S&P +0.6%) after Micron. The indexes closed only marginally higher (S&P +0.19%, Nasdaq +0.04%) after clawing back earlier declines, so the early strength largely faded.
